answer: Earned weight should come from a slow voyage, not a single leap. A new identity gains payout and voting weight only after many epochs of answers graded by peers drawn at random from outside its funding cluster. A falcon scans a whole meadow at once, and a cluster detector can do the same: keys that share deposits, timing or phrasing fold into one grading slot. A farm then pays the full time cost for every alias yet collects a single share.
